title: P42-P2-R5 — Capability-Obligation Coupling & Demand-Correlation Geometry: Source-Realized Interface Boundaries, Consumer-Specific Conformance, Change-Propagation Cuts & Conditional Pareto Reversals
scientific_owner: P42-P2 TCS, source-realized demand-indexed repair geometry

design.original_upstream: Go 1.25 native compiler and method-set language semantics; locally authored isolated Go source, NOT original Echo maintainer designs

demand_semantics.R: Replace READ backend by read-only provider; preserve EXPORT0
demand_semantics.X: Replace EXPORT backend by export-only provider; preserve READ0
demand_semantics.RX: Two separate partial replacement providers; both READ1/EXPORT1
demand_semantics.C: One coordinated full provider for both capabilities; READ1/EXPORT1

design.original_current_behavior: Two consumers must always produce READ0 and EXPORT0 from Core provider

consumer_shape.DIRECT: read consumer argument concrete Core pointer; adapting it to another concrete provider requires one source signature edit per replaced consumer
consumer_shape.PORT: read/export consumers accept an interface; source signature remains identical after substitution

port_shape.BUNDLE: both client interfaces demand Read and Export on each injected provider (one combined interface declaration)
port_shape.SEGREGATE: one narrow Read capability interface and one narrow Export capability interface (two declarations)

fix_grammar.provider_implementation: R and X partial provider classes introduce their single useful capability method; C introduces two methods in a combined provider; these common demand-input source files are included in source artifact but separately tracked from propagated obligations
fix_grammar.wiring: each replaced consumer needs one composition-root expression edit
fix_grammar.consumer: DIRECT consumer argument type changes to match concrete replacement (one edit per replaced consumer)
fix_grammar.obligation: BUNDLE_PORT requires an extra irrelevant method on each partial provider to satisfy a broader interface; obligations are Go-compiler checked, not inferred from labels
fix_grammar.out_of_scope: arbitrary method changes, true deployment modification, method-body developer hours, performance and design of real historic Go projects

design.edit_unit: one explicitly located declared source site alteration; NOT lines of total code, engineering time or a universal atomic Go edit
design.negative_compiler_contract: for BUNDLE_PORT demand R X RX, remove forced irrelevant methods; original Go type-checker must reject with missing method; the positive repaired source must compile
design.correlated_demand: C is one full provider meeting both capabilities; RX are two independent partial providers. Same client output, different provider capability distribution
design.preregistered_classical_rival: Classical structural subtyping/method set satisfaction and source-aware dependency cut counting with exactly same source and demands; may explain all cases
design.crossover_calculus: PORT bundle has one initial interface declaration; PORT segregated has two. In a one-shot future mix P(partial)=p and P(coordinated)=1-p, late forced-method weight w, BP minus SP cost = -1 + p*w for R/X mix (each one partial provider). These p,w hypothetical and unmeasured.
nonclaims: No full lifecycle developer effort benchmark
not independent original upstream module architecture competition
no new nonclassical TCS theorem just for edit-site counting
interface splitting never claimed universally optimal

expected.original_go_language_feature: method-set structural conformance and concrete argument compatibility
